corridor_floor_h.png.use: horizontal corridor cells (walls N and S)
corridor_floor_h.png.rule: variant = thash(x,y) % 6 (4 = moss in a joint, 5 = dust drift: use sparingly)

corridor_floor_v.png.use: vertical corridor cells (walls W and E) and junctions

corridor_lip_n.png.use: wall cell directly NORTH of a horizontal corridor cell: draw this INSTEAD of the 14 px front face, at the face position (X, Y_raised + 16). With the raised top it fills down to the wall cell's bottom edge, so the corridor's full 16 px stays visible

corridor_rim_s.png.use: wall cell directly SOUTH of a horizontal corridor cell: draw that wall top WITHOUT the 8 px raise (it otherwise covers half the corridor), then this rim at its top edge (X, y*16 + TOP)

corridor_rim_w.png.use: west wall of a vertical corridor: replaces the 8 px side face; draw at the corridor cell's left edge (x*16, y*16 + TOP)

corridor_rim_e.png.use: east wall of a vertical corridor: replaces the 8 px side face; draw at the corridor cell's right edge (x*16 + 13, y*16 + TOP)

corridor_ao.png.use: optional contact shadow inside the corridor cell on each side that touches a wall (replaces the bake's generic AO there)

why: a 1-wide corridor is currently covered by the north wall's 14 px face (6 px into the cell) plus the south wall's 8 px raised top, leaving about 2 px of floor. In vertical corridors the 8 px side faces from both walls cover the cell. The pieces above shrink those overlaps to a 3 px rim
detection:
corridor cells (computed once per room, after FURN remaps):
  W(x,y) = grid cell is a wall ('#' or '='); outside the grid counts as NOT wall (it is an exit), so the void between corridor walls at the grid edge is not picked up; F(x,y) = room['walk'][y][x]
  horizontal corridor cell: F(x,y) and W(x,y-1) and W(x,y+1)                                  (1 wide)
                         or F(x,y) and W(x,y-1) and F(x,y+1) and W(x,y+2)   (+ the cell below)  (2 wide)
  vertical corridor cell:   F(x,y) and W(x-1,y) and W(x+1,y)                                  (1 wide)
                         or F(x,y) and W(x-1,y) and F(x+1,y) and W(x+2,y)   (+ the cell right)  (2 wide)
  plus: extend each run by one cell into the room (the doorway mouth) so the runner meets the room floor; skip cells holding stairs/doors/props.
  a cell that is both (corner/junction): use the _v sheet.
lighting: no emissive or baked light; darkness/lamp rules apply unchanged (the runner is only a lighter and warmer albedo)
